# Psalm 41 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. A psalm of David.

**2** Blessed is the one who considers the poor! In the day of trouble the LORD delivers him;

**3** the LORD protects him and keeps him alive; he is called blessed in the land; You do not give him up to the will of his enemies.

**4** The LORD sustains him on his sickbed; in his illness You restore him to full health.

**5** As for me, I said, 'O LORD, be gracious to me; heal me, for I have sinned against You!'

**6** My enemies say of me in malice, 'When will he die, and his name perish?'

**7** And when one comes to see me, he utters empty words, while his heart gathers iniquity; when he goes out, he tells it abroad.

**8** All who hate me whisper together about me; they imagine the worst for me.

**9** 'A deadly thing is poured out on him; he will not rise again from where he lies.'

**10** Even my close friend in whom I trusted, who ate my bread, has lifted his heel against me.

**11** But You, O LORD, be gracious to me, and raise me up, that I may repay them!

**12** By this I know that You delight in me: my enemy will not shout in triumph over me.

**13** But You have upheld me because of my integrity, and set me in Your presence forever.

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **41:13**: This doxology closes Book I of the Psalter (Psalms 1-41). The five-book division mirrors the five books of Torah.

— LOGOS
